cards.text: Before any angels show up, Luke writes to a man he calls most excellent Theophilus. He says many have already composed an account of "the things that have been fulfilled among us," handed down by the people who saw them with their own eyes. EYEWITNESSES, friend, not somebody's cousin's coworker's group chat.

cards.question: Luke wants to write his own orderly account for Theophilus. What does Luke do before he writes it?

answers.text: He investigates everything from the beginning
He waits for a sign from heaven first
He copies the oldest account he finds

cards.question: Luke writes his account so Theophilus may know the ___ of the things he has been taught.

cards.text: Now the story begins, in the time of Herod king of Judea. There's a priest named Zechariah from the priestly division of Abijah, and his wife Elizabeth is a descendant of Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14).

cards.question: Zechariah the priest and his wife Elizabeth. True or false: they struggle to keep the commandments of the Lord.

cards.text: But this good couple has a hard road. They have no children, because Elizabeth is barren, and they're both well along in years.
One day Zechariah's division is on duty, and he's serving as priest before God. Somebody's about to go into the temple of the Lord to burn incense.

cards.question: How is Zechariah picked to go into the temple of the Lord and burn incense?
While Zechariah is inside burning incense, the whole congregation is outside. True or false: they're praying.

cards.text: I bet Zechariah walked in expecting smoke, not COMPANY. Just then an angel of the Lord appears, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.

cards.question: An angel of the Lord just appeared beside the altar of incense. How does Zechariah react?

answers.text: He is startled and gripped with fear
He bows and asks the angel's name
He calmly finishes burning the incense

cards.text: Then the angel speaks: 'Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard.' Heard, friend. Not left on read.

cards.question: The angel tells Zechariah his prayer has been heard. True or false: the angel says Elizabeth will bear Zechariah a son.
The angel tells Zechariah to give his son the name ___.

cards.text: And this boy is no ordinary baby. He'll be a joy and delight to his dad, many will rejoice at his birth, and he'll be great in the sight of the Lord.

cards.question: The angel says John will never take wine or strong drink. What will John be filled with, even from his mother's womb?

cards.text: Then the angel tells what John will do. He'll turn many of the sons of Israel back to the Lord their God, and he'll go on before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah the prophet (1 Kings 18:36).

cards.question: The angel says John will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children. Who will John turn to the wisdom of the righteous?
The angel says John will go on before the Lord to make ready a ___ prepared for the Lord.

cards.text: Zechariah is looking right at an ANGEL, and he asks, 'How can I be sure of this?' That's me standing in front of an oven at full blast asking, 'Is it on?'

cards.question: Zechariah asks the angel how he can be sure of this. What reason does Zechariah give?

answers.text: He and his wife are both old
He has never seen an angel before
No priest has ever heard this before

cards.text: 'I am Gabriel,' the angel replies. He tells Zechariah he stands in the presence of God and was sent to bring him this good news.

cards.question: Gabriel says Zechariah did not believe his words. What will happen to Zechariah?

answers.text: He will be silent and unable to speak
He will be blind until the boy is born
He will lose his place as a priest

cards.question: True or false: Gabriel says Zechariah's silence ends as soon as he leaves the temple.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the people outside are waiting and wondering why he's taking so long in the temple. You know the feeling: a coworker says 'be right back,' and an hour later you're still staring at the door.

cards.question: Zechariah finally comes out and can't speak to the people. True or false: they realize he has seen a vision in the temple.

cards.text: So Zechariah keeps making signs to them. A priest playing charades for the whole crowd, and the clue is ANGEL. Try acting THAT out.
When his days of service are complete, Zechariah goes home. After these days, Elizabeth becomes pregnant and stays in seclusion for five months.

cards.question: Elizabeth is pregnant at last, and she says the Lord has shown her favor. What does she say He has taken away?

cards.text: Elizabeth declares, 'The Lord has done this for me.' Now hold on to your apron, friend, because this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then the angel speaks: '...heard.'", "Heard, friend." and "Not left on read." Only the passage's opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "So Zechariah keeps making signs to them.", "A priest playing charades for the whole crowd, and the clue is ANGEL." and "Try acting THAT out."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 18 already asked about the end of Elizabeth's statement in Luke 1:25 (favor, disgrace taken away). Card 19 then steps back to the first words of the same verse ('The Lord has done this for me.'). This moves backward through the passage instead of forward. The quote should come on a story card before card 18, and the last card can be just the 'story's not over' line.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The Holy Spirit' stands out from the two wrong answers. Both wrong answers share one pattern ('Great wisdom', 'Great strength'), so the right one is the odd one out and sounds more like the Bible.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The disobedient' is two words. Both wrong answers are four-word phrases ('The priests of the temple', 'The rulers of the nations'). The short right answer stands out by length.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Card 1 states as fact that Luke is the one writing ('Luke writes to a man he calls most excellent Theophilus'). Luke 1:1-4 never names its author, and no verse anywhere in Scripture names Luke as the writer of this book, so the card cannot carry a reference for this fact. The rules allow outside facts like 'who wrote a letter, with their reference', and require that 'Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.' The passage title also uses 'Luke's Purpose.'
findings.question: When a book's traditional author is not named in Scripture (here, Luke for the Gospel of Luke), may Papa Dorin name that author as fact without a reference? Or should he say something like 'the writer' or 'Luke, as he's traditionally known'?
